newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PETROL PRICES TO RISE BY UP TO 2 PCT-ANALYST.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PETROL PRICES TO RISE BY UP TO 2 PCT-ANALYST.

text.p: Petrol retail prices in Poland are unlikely to rise by more than two percent after the recent and planned increases by producers, an independent fuel market monitoring agency said on Thursday.

Michal Bichniewicz, analyst at Brog Services agency, told Reuters the wholesale price rise of end-July and early August has so far not been reflected in retail price growth. Prices at fuel stations could change as of next week, he said.

"Prices at stations have been stable as of June, the recent producers' price increases have so far not been reflected in retail prices, but this should change as early as next week," Bichniewicz said.

"If the current tendencies (fuel price increases worldwide and the dollar strenghtening against the zloty) are sustained, the increase should not exceed two or three groszes (0.02-0.03 zloty) per litre, or two percent," he added.
Poland's largest fuel distributor, the state-owned CPN SA, confirmed the price should not rise more than by two percent.
"I think the prices would not go up by more than one to three groszes per litre," Barbara Hodbod of CPN's price department said.

Petrochemia Plock and Rafineria Gdansk refineries, supplying about 80 percent of the country's fuel market, increased prices in July by about one to three groszes, depending on a petrol brand, per litre.
Earlier this week, they upped the prices by another one to two groszes per litre.
A source at Petrochemia said the refinery might further increase its petrol price because crude oil price has grown on the world markets and the dollar has strenghtened.
According to Brog Services, fuel prices rose by five to 13 percent, depending on brands, since they were freed in February 1997. The 95-octance unleaded petrol now cost 1.68 zloty.
